trickyParts: Referrer-Policy is same-origin, not no-referrer: under no-referrer a browser sends Origin: null on the page's own form posts, which the exact-origin check refuses.

The account switch is a GET link (/approve/<record>?switch=1), and a lapsed POST answers a page with a link rather than a redirect: the page's form-action 'self' governs a form submission's redirect, so a 302 to the provider would be blocked.

GET /approve/{record} checks the id's shape, then the session, then the record. The sign-in names the record's approver as login_hint when a record has that id, which A1 requires, and names nobody for an id no record has, so the hint is the one way the two redirects differ; a record id is a SHA-256 hash, so a caller that can name one already holds it.

The two decide routes authenticate inside the handler, so they spend the shared per-address rate-limit bucket themselves: moving them off accountAuth had left that bucket unspent, which would have let an unauthenticated caller drive one database read per request.

main took migration number 0020 while the branch held one, which TestMigrationSetIsNumberedOneToN refuses and which would stop the broker from starting. The branch forward-merged main a second time and renumbered to 0021 and 0022.
